segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 408 HKD is a strong bargain for a flexible friend group that can use this departure, and it turns a possible escape into a real plan. I am very price-sensitive and this destination has little pull, but the low fare itself makes the optional trip worthwhile. I would still pay the 510 HKD normal fare if the member quota ran out.

analysis.summary: At the 408 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Four declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and five were voluntary low-interest or destination-appeal declines, not price objections. Buyers repeatedly called 408 a bargain, and several would have paid the 510 regular fare. No customer cited the fare itself as too high. The current price sits at the permitted cap, so there is no room to test higher.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 408 HKD member fare on fresh customers will reproduce a weighted conversion near 0.38, with declines driven mainly by availability and low trip interest rather than fare objections.

analysis.summary: Seven of sixteen members bought at the 408 fare, citing strong value and destination appeal; several would also pay the 510 regular fare. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced with no available ticket, and three were low destination interest or optional-trip apathy rather than price objections. No customer primarily objected to the fare itself. Evidence supports testing the same fare on fresh customers, though the cap of 408 limits upward testing and the inventory-forced declines add uncertainty.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 408 fare on fresh members will yield a weighted conversion not materially below the observed 0.44, with declines driven mainly by unavailable inventory rather than fare level.

analysis.summary: At the 295 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. All seven declines cite low trip interest or casual browsing rather than fare objections; one decline is inventory-forced. Buyers repeatedly describe the fare as a bargain, and several would not pay the 510 HKD regular fare. No customer objects to the 295 HKD price itself, so the evidence does not support lowering the fare. The cap of 408 HKD leaves room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts relative to 295 HKD, because current buyers describe the fare as well below their stated ceilings and no decline cites price.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 346 HKD member fare, 4 of 16 members bought, generating 1384 HKD in basic receipts. Eight declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections. Five declines cited low trip interest or a strong outside option despite finding the fare affordable. The four buyers called the fare compelling or a bargain, and two would have declined the 510 HKD regular fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will not reduce weighted conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because buyers described the fare as compelling and no decline cited price as the main reason.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

Three declines were inventory/budget-forced. Several buyers said they would not pay the 510 normal fare, and some would pay it. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers to see if enough purchases remain, since the cap is 408 and current price is below it.

analysis.summary: Nine of sixteen members bought at the 394 HKD fare, mostly citing strong value and destination appeal; several would also pay the 510 HKD regular fare. Five declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest optional-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer primarily declined because the fare was too high. The paired initial at 408 HKD showed lower weighted revenue than the current 394 HKD fare, so the evidence leans toward testing a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough member purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at least as high as at 394 HKD, since no cited customer primarily declined on price.

analysis.summary: At the current 320 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain, several noting they would still pay the 510 HKD regular fare. Four declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were low-interest or recent-trip objections rather than price objections. No customer explicitly rejected the fare as too expensive. Evidence points to strong value at the current price, but buying at 320 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because several current buyers stated they would pay the 510 HKD regular fare.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
